title: fix(spec): judge a nested RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR row instead of ignoring it
body:
Fixes #17969

Clause-②: yes

## What was broken, and the reading that says so

`check:authorable-surface` builds `currentKeys` from `schema.properties` **one level deep**
(`packages/spec/scripts/build-schemas.ts`). Check (b2) — the guard that refuses a
`RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR` entry naming a key the build still emits as LIVE — consults that map, so a
**dotted** row matched nothing in it and was silently ignored rather than judged. 48 of the shipped
rows are dotted.

Reproduced on this branch before the fix, by ablation, with the card's own controls:

| probe | pre-fix `check:authorable-surface` |
|:--|:--|
| fabricated nested row `system/SchemaLevelIsolationStrategy:performance.zzNotARealKey9999` | **exit 0**, zero failures |
| lit control: `system/SchemaLevelIsolationStrategy:strategy`, a live top-level key | **exit 1**, refused |

## The coupling, measured before the fix was written

Three lines below `currentKeys` the same map is `currentEntries`, the **published**
authorable-surface baseline. The dispatch asked for a measurement rather than an argument, so:

1. **Does widening `currentKeys` in place move `authorable-surface/**`?** Measured, not reasoned:
   the one-level loop was replaced with a recursive walk, `gen:schema` was run, and the diff read
   **+14,376 lines across all 14 shards** (`ai 320, api 6099, automation 496, data 1393,
   identity 83, integration 170, kernel 1997, marketplace 86, qa 93, security 90, shared 6,
   studio 187, system 1648, ui 1709`). The script was then restored byte-identical
   (`git hash-object` back to `b4f0ac58c00086a60528b88acdf1c45f13115387`, `git diff HEAD` empty).
   So yes: widening in place publishes the whole nested key space as a ratcheted, author-facing
   contract.
2. **Is a nested view consulted only by the checker sufficient?** Yes, and that is what shipped.
   `currentKeys` and `currentEntries` are untouched; the nested state is resolved for the
   **registered rows only** and reaches nothing that emits. Deliberately no nested map is
   materialised — the hazard here is a nested key space lying around for a later author to pipe
   into `currentEntries`, so there is nothing to pipe.
3. **Does the published surface have to move?** No. `git diff --exit-code -- packages/spec/authorable-surface/`
   is clean after a full `gen:schema` on this branch, and `check:generated` reports all 15 generated
   artifacts up to date.

## What the change does to each check that reads `currentKeys`

- **(a0) lost by a declared rename** — unchanged. Reads `currentKeys`, which is byte-for-byte what
  it was.
- **(a) a key that vanished outright** — unchanged, and deliberately so: it would otherwise start
  reporting every nested key as "vanished" against a baseline that has never recorded one.
- **(b) live to retired must be registered** — unchanged. It still demands a row only for a
  TOP-LEVEL transition, so no nested retirement that owes nothing today starts owing one. This is
  the behaviour change the card itself flagged under its shape 1, and it is not made here.
- **(b2) an entry naming a key still LIVE** — now reaches nested rows. A top-level row is judged on
  the same expression and the same message as before; a nested row is judged on the resolved state
  of its path.
- **(b3), new — an entry naming a nested path this build does not emit.** For a TOP-LEVEL key that
  state is the aged-out steady state (b2) exempts: the tombstone carried `[RETIRED]`, aged two
  majors, and check (c) let its baseline line go, with evidence at every step. A nested key reaches
  none of that — it has no baseline line, no mark and no aging clock — so no gated route can produce
  a registered nested row whose path is absent, and the one origin left is that the row is wrong.
- **A row whose whole DEF this build does not emit stays unjudged**, exactly as today: that is the
  `RETIRED_DEFS_BY_MAJOR` steady state, adjudicated by the `json-schema.manifest/` ratchet. Three
  of the 48 nested rows are in it (the change-management family, retired whole).

## Population, which the card recorded as unmeasured

Censused over the 48 dotted rows the shipped table declares: **45 resolve to a tombstone, 3 name a
def this build does not emit, 0 resolve LIVE, 0 fail to resolve.** The gate is green on the shipped
table, and the sixth test case below keeps that measured rather than assumed.

## Acceptance — a probe, a lit control, and two dark controls

Pinned end to end in `scripts/build-schemas-check-mode.test.ts`, spawned against the real generator
in a sandbox that substitutes its own `RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR`:

| case | expected | why it is here |
|:--|:--|:--|
| PROBE — the card's fabricated nested row | refused, exit 1 | the run the card measured at exit 0 |
| LIT CONTROL — a live TOP-LEVEL key | refused, same message class | the guard that worked must not regress |
| a live NESTED key | refused by (b2) | the row the top-level-only map could never see |
| a live TOP-LEVEL key whose own NAME carries a dot | refused by (b2), not (b3) | routing asks the schema, not the spelling |
| DARK CONTROL — a real nested retirement | passes, exit 0 | a checker that refused every dotted row would pass the probe too |
| DARK CONTROL — a fabricated row under a def this build does not emit | passes, exit 0 | absence waived by the DEF's state, never by the path being real |
| the shipped table, seeded whole | passes, exit 0 | the population, kept measured |

**Reverse verification.** With the fix committed, `packages/spec/scripts/build-schemas.ts` was
restored to its pre-fix bytes (`git restore --source=BASE`, on-disk hash verified equal to the base
blob, `nestedStates` occurrences 3 to 0) and the block re-run: **exactly 2 of 7 cases go red — the
PROBE and the live-NESTED case, both on `expected +0 to be 1`, i.e. the gate exiting 0.** The five
controls stay green. Restored afterwards with `git checkout HEAD --`; `git diff HEAD` empty and the
on-disk blob back to `4948f991ee792944f90e91747054950bf7726fe7`.

**A discovery from the first run of the new pins**, recorded because it moved the design: the
published baseline carries **4 dotted keys that are TOP-LEVEL property names containing a dot** —
`api/ODataResponse:@odata.context` and two siblings, and a SCIM extension URN on
`identity/SCIMUser`. So "has a dot" is not the same question as "names a path": routing asks the
emitted schema first and reads a row as a path only when this build emits no top-level property of
that exact name. A fifth test case and an enumerated roster pin it, and the roster is also what a
widened published surface would blow up. A second discovery, from the resolver's own unit pins:
**36 of the emitted refs are spelled `#`** (a recursive schema pointing at its own document), which
the first cut read as external and would have reported as a typo'd path.

## Evidence

```
pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:authorable-surface   exit 0
pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated            exit 0   all 15 generated artifacts up to date
pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:api-surface          exit 0   public API surface + factory signatures unchanged
pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:docs                 exit 0   224 generated files in sync
pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck                  exit 0   tsc + check:scripts-typecheck + check:test-typecheck
pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test                       exit 0   485 files, 13835 tests
pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test:repo                  exit 0   31 files, 536 tests
node scripts/pm/check-widening-tells.mjs --declaration yes --diff BRANCH.diff   exit 0
git diff --exit-code -- packages/spec/authorable-surface/  exit 0   published surface byte-identical
```

ESLint, narrowed and declared: `pnpm exec eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the 4 files
this branch touches — **4 files linted, 0 errors, 0 warnings**, file count read from the JSON
report. The universe eslint itself configures is `**/*.{ts,tsx,mts,cts,js,jsx,mjs,cjs}` minus
`NEVER_LINTED`, read from `eslint.config.mjs`; and the narrowing is sound because that config
**never enables type-aware linting for any file** (no `parserOptions.project`, no typed
`@typescript-eslint` rules — the config says so in its own measured note), so this diff cannot move
the verdict on a file it does not touch. The repo-wide sweep is CI's.

Gate families, derived from the real change set rather than from the dispatch list
(`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`): **59 derived, 28 run here
with recorded exit codes, 1 NOT MEASURED** (`check:type-check-debt` exits 3 — it refuses without a
whole-repo build closure, which is CI's), **1 not measured by a runner cap**
(`check:pm-dispatch-gates`, killed at 420s by this seat's own `timeout`), **30 declared to CI** —
cross-cutting families this 4-file spec-scripts diff cannot move.

## File surface

- `packages/spec/scripts/build-schemas.ts` — the routing, (b2)'s nested limb, (b3), and `isRetired`
  delegating to one definition of the tombstone predicate.
- `packages/spec/scripts/lib/nested-authorable-keys.ts` — new. The resolution rules, and the
  authority on what they cannot see.
- `packages/spec/scripts/nested-authorable-keys.test.ts` — new. 17 unit pins on the resolver.
- `packages/spec/scripts/build-schemas-check-mode.test.ts` — the 7 acceptance cases above.

Untouched, as declared at claim time: `packages/spec/authorable-surface/**` (byte-identical),
`packages/spec/scripts/lib/renamed-defs.ts`, and the `RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR` registry — the two
ablations that wrote to the tree were restored byte-identical and proved so.

**No changeset, `skip-changeset`.** Measured rather than assumed: `@objectstack/spec` ships
`files[]` = dist, json-schema, liveness, prompts, llms.txt, README.md, `src/**/*.zod.ts`,
CHANGELOG.md, api-surface, spec-changes.json — `scripts/` is not in it, and neither `bin` nor
`exports` reaches it. Grepping the built published paths for every symbol this diff adds
(`nestedAuthorableKeyState`, `isNestedAuthorableKey`, `isRetiredJsonSchemaNode`,
`unresolvableNested`, `nested-authorable-keys`) returns **0 files each**, against positive controls
that return 8 (`SchemaLevelIsolationStrategySchema`) and 25 (`RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR`).

## On the `Clause-②: yes` declaration

Declared `yes` conservatively at claim time, because the honest answer depended on the measurement
above. The delivered diff **leaves the published authorable surface byte-identical** and only gives
a checker a discrimination it lacked over a class of inputs; nothing an author may write changes,
and nothing published moves. That is the evidence, stated plainly — the contract review decides the
declaration, and this PR does not lower it.

## Acceptance notes

- **The `RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR` docblock now under-describes its own gate by one state.** Its
  "Lifecycle" paragraph says "The one state the gate rejects is an entry naming a key that is still
  LIVE", and after this change a nested row has a second rejected state. The registry was declared
  read-only for this card, so it is not edited here: a one-paragraph follow-up, noted rather than
  filed.
- **`check:cross-package-test-inputs` reds in a worktree that has a built `packages/spec/dist/`.**
  Measured here with a control: this branch reds it (naming `packages/cli/test/init-created-files-summary.e2e.test.ts`
  walking `packages/spec/dist/`, a radius no declared glob reaches), while the same gate on a
  checkout with no `packages/spec/dist/` exits 0. Independent of this diff, which touches neither
  `packages/cli/**` nor any declaration the gate reads. Two readings and both are worth a card: a
  gate whose verdict depends on local build state, or a true finding CI cannot see because it runs
  the gate without that build. Reported for filing rather than filed.
- This branch is based on `e81c4e5f30` and `main` has moved since; the merge and CI convergence are
  the seat's, per the dispatch contract.
